parsed.explanation: No criminalisation of trans identity, but the operative regime stacks several traveller-facing exposures. Entry adjudication is the sharpest: the national sex redefinition, halt on X-marked passports, and February 2025 cable directing officers to refuse where documents cast doubt on an applicant's sex, with possible lifetime ineligibility, have drawn advisories from eight governments after detentions. Facilities access is restricted in government buildings nationally and by one of the country's most severe municipal ordinances here. Custody is documented hostile: a trans woman with a female licence marker was jailed in a men's facility under a male guard and denied hospital care after a mob beating over restroom use — a beating where both victims were charged and no attacker was arrested. National hate-crime coverage and pending litigation are real but unproven locally. This sits below jurisdictions with functioning protections and above those where trans identity itself draws imprisonment.

entry_documents.exposure: National order defines sex as birth-assigned; new passports/visas may not self-select markers; X markers no longer issued. Feb 2025 cable tells posts to refuse where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and weigh material-misrepresentation lifetime ineligibility. Foreign governments issued advisories after detentions of trans travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marked passports stay valid until expiry; the passport policy is under challenge in national courts; a legal-aid FAQ covers document rules for trans travellers.
entry_documents.interaction: Document check at visa/entry feeds directly into refusal, secondary screening, or (never automatic) a fraud finding; refusal strands the traveller abroad with no local remedy.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented locally: a trans woman was held in a men's facility and searched by a male guard despite a female licence marker, and was denied hospital care. Nationally, corrections policies strip hormones and mandate psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented as operating for trans detainees; national prison LGBTQ order was rescinded and reporting of trans prisoner numbers stopped.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facilities and custody actors ignore foreign/state markers when deciding housing and search procedure; an ordinary incident or arrest converts a document mismatch into birth-sex custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Gender-congruent facility use barred in government buildings across many states nationally; the relevant municipality enacted one of the country's most severe restroom ordinances, and a mob attack over restroom use followed. Statewide position on facilities is not established by the sources.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Two municipalities bar gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; nothing documented at state level.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Municipal ordinance plus absent state protection means a facility dispute escalates to police and charges against the trans person, not the complainant.

care_services.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned since January 2024 after veto override; transition care excluded from insurance and the low-income programme; a trans person was refused hospital care in the documented August 2026 incident.
care_services.protection: National insurance-coverage restrictions are proposed, not final, and some executive orders are enjoined.
care_services.interaction: An emergency (injury, assault) becomes an outing to medics with no guaranteed congruent ward placement; a travelling family cannot obtain minor care in-state.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'rapid identification and neutralization' of groups described as radically pro-transgender; a DOJ reward memorandum invokes 'radical gender ideology'; officials frame minor care as mutilation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; national 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises the odds that police contact, protest attendance or visible advocacy is escalated rather than de-escalated; no documented prosecution of a visitor on this basis.

minors_guardians.exposure: State ban on blockers, hormones and surgery for minors; national order directs investigating schools and prosecuting teachers who use a trans minor's name/pronouns; sports exclusion orders. A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces care denial and a hostile institutional climate.
minors_guardians.protection: Several national orders are enjoined or under litigation; no state protection for the minor's care or expression.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian seeking care or school engagement for a trans minor crosses from visitor status into conduct the state frames as harm to a child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: August 2026 mob beating of a trans couple over restroom use; both victims charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker arrested, plea unsigned; the state hate-crime statute omits gender identity. Per-capita killing figures are explicitly undercount floors and near-identical to the 'safest' state, so carry no magnitude.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute reaches gender-identity bias and is the prosecutorial route here; two municipal non-discrimination ordinances.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police arriving at a harassment complaint have documented treating the trans target as the offender, converting victimhood into custody exposure.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state law bars gender-identity discrimination in employment, housing or accommodations; the 1997 hate-crime statute excludes gender identity; the dormant sodomy statute remains (unenforced).
remedies_unknowns.protection: National employment-discrimination ruling, national hate-crime statute, pending passport and executive-order litigation, and a legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists on paper nationally but the one documented local test (attackers unarrested, victims charged) shows it not operating for a trans person on the ground.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.45-A is document friction only: denied boarding, no detention, no violence, and an ombudsman that at least accepts complaints. This jurisdiction is materially worse — possible entry refusal with lifetime-ineligibility exposure, documented mob violence with victims charged, and birth-sex custody placement — so it sits below that anchor.

0.25-A describes coercive custody cycles, extortion and humiliation with no law against trans identity. This jurisdiction is better on state predation (no extortion pattern, existing X passports honoured, functioning courts, national hate-crime coverage) but worse on documented communal violence tolerated by police and on cross-sex custody searches; the net is close to, slightly above, that anchor.

0.65-B has a binding directorate rule protecting chosen names and correcting records after friction; the protection functions. Here no comparable operating protection exists for facilities, custody or care, and the documented local case shows state actors overriding a valid female marker, so this jurisdiction sits far below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is not criminalisation of trans identity but a set of enforced, traveller-facing frictions. Border adjudication can refuse or strand a traveller whose documents cast doubt on sex, with a possible lifetime fraud finding. Once inside, facilities rules at municipal and national-building level, a surgery-only marker regime, and documented custody practice (men's housing and male-guard search despite a female marker, care denial) mean any incident escalates into birth-sex treatment by institutions. Street violence is documented and the state's response is the damning part: attackers unarrested, victims charged. National hate-crime and employment protections are real but were not shown operating locally; litigation creates uncertainty in both directions and is not treated as protection.
